children: Personal computing and printing company HP
will be announcing earnings results this Tuesday afternoon. Here’s what investors should know.

HP beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $15.68 billion, up 12.5% year on year. It was an exceptional quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates and a solid beat of analysts’ EPS guidance for next quarter estimates.
Is HP a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting HP’s revenue to grow 3.5% year on year, in line with the 4.2% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. HP has a history of exceeding Wall Street’s expectations.

Looking at HP’s peers in the hardware & infrastructure segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Super Micro delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 298%, beating analysts’ expectations by 18.6%, and IonQ reported revenues up 336%, topping estimates by 37%. Super Micro traded down 5.7% following the results while IonQ was up 23.4%.

Over the last year or so, investors' attention has moved from one major market theme to the next, spanning AI disruption and surging infrastructure investment to geopolitical tensions, interest rates, and the health of the broader economy. While some of the hardware & infrastructure stocks have shown solid performance in this choppy environment, the group has generally underperformed, with share prices down 9.4% on average over the last month. HP is down 17.5% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $27.55 (compared to the current share price of $28.13).
